text.tspan: CigiStarter - a CIGI 3.3 Image Generator

A minimal replacement for the Master IG PC: wakes the HOST with SOF, answers its HAT/HOT requests from the terrain Prepar3D will actually fly the aircraft onto (the PdkTerrainProbe add-on), falls back to an offline SRTM database and then to the sim over FSUIPC, and fans the HOST's downstream stream out to the extra IG PCs. CIGI 3.3, UDP, little-endian. Single Win32 binary, runs unelevated, streams from launch with the
window minimised.
1 - The link: HOST, IG, extra IG PCs
Deployment defaults: hardcoded in src\main.cpp
--host-ip / --host-port / --ig-ip / --ig-port
exist for a bench test only; the deployment
passes none of them
flight model, owns the frame rate
receives SOF on :8001
sends flight data from :8000
IG - CigiStarter 192.168.70.70
binds 0.0.0.0:8000 for flight data
rides HAT/HOT responses on the SOF stream
UDP 8000, passive:
nothing ever comes back
SOF - id 101, 24 B - the request that wakes the HOST
flight data: IGCtrl - EntityCtrl x3 - HAT/HOT Request - ViewCtrl - ArticPart x5 - RateCtrl x8
one copy per datagram
The copies keep the HOST's own address and port as
their source (192.168.70.2:8001), so a client's
bridge needs no reconfiguration: it sees exactly
the stream it would have seen as the IG.
Downstream HOST -> IG :8000 IGCtrl - EntityCtrl x3 - HAT/HOT Request - ViewCtrl - ArticPart x5 - RateCtrl x8 - Atmosphere (warm-up)
Upstream IG -> HOST :8001 SOF id 101 (+ the HAT/HOT responses, ids 102/103, when answering)
Fan-out HOST -> each client one copy of every downstream datagram, labelled with the HOST's source
2 - The per-frame loop
IG (CigiStarter)
HOST
SOF, frame N
one datagram per SOF
The HOST is a request/response slave: it sends nothing until the IG sends a Start-of-Frame. Each SOF is answered with one datagram
carrying:
IG Control x1 - Entity Control x3 - HAT/HOT Request x1 - View Control x1
Articulated Part Control x5 - Rate Control x8
Atmosphere Control x1 (first frames only, warm-up)
The SOF echoes the HOST's own frame counter at offset 8 - never a count of the SOFs the IG sent - so the outgoing SOF stays
byte-identical to the reference Master's.
3 - Protocol and wire layout (CIGI 3.3, little-endian)
framing: [id 1B][size 1B][payload] size = total bytes incl. header
SOF id 101 (0x65), 24 bytes
65 18 03 00 00 b5 00 80 <frame counter> 00 00 00 00 00 .. 00 the reference
| | +-- 0x00 0x80 at bytes 6-7: the byte-swap flag (little-endian)
| +----- byte 5: IG mode (bits 0-1), timestamp-valid (2), earth
| model (3), CIGI minor version (4-7); 3.3 => 0x30
offset 8: the HOST's frame counter, echoed out of the IG Control it arrived in
offsets 12 / 16: timestamp and last-host-frame - left at 0 by the reference
Master, still 0 here, which is what keeps the SOF byte-identical
the IG never picks its own mode: byte 5 becomes 0x31 (Operate) as soon as the
HOST commands Operate; --ig-mode only seeds it before the first IG Control
HAT/HOT Request -> Response id 102, 16 B: Height double @ 8
types 0 (HAT) / 1 (HOT)
-> Extended Response id 103, 40 B: HAT @ 8, HOT @ 16
type 2 (extended)
both carry a 3-byte reserved gap after the flags byte, which is what aligns
the first double to an 8-byte boundary. CIGI 3.2 packed them straight after
the flags: the HOST then read HOT out of the material-code bytes - zero -
and flew the aircraft down to the terrain.
HAT = request altitude - HOT, which is what catches the two doubles packed in the wrong place. Valid is set only when a terrain source could
answer.
Pacing uses timeBeginPeriod(1): Windows' default 15.6 ms (~64 Hz) timer granularity otherwise caps any rate above ~60 Hz at ~64 with an
occasional burst - worth knowing when comparing rates with another tool.
In Host-Master.pcapng the counter advances ~0.52 per SOF (~53 Hz) while the SOF rate was ~100 Hz (an 8/12 ms alternation): the Master asked for
about twice the replies the HOST had frames to give.
4 - HAT/HOT answering: three sources, one anchor
1 - Prepar3D's own terrain, through PdkTerrainProbe.dll
ISurfaceQueryManagerV400, a free-standing query: the surface the sim will place the aircraft on, so runway flattening and any added scenery
are included and nothing has to be pre-mapped
2 - the SRTM terrain database, offline .hgt tiles
answered from latitude and longitude alone, so it stays correct for the whole flight, but it is a copy of the world: no flattening, no changed
scenery
3 - the local Prepar3D via FSUIPC 0x0020
the ground under the sim's own aircraft: one point only, so it can stand in only for a request where that aircraft is
HOT = the height from the first source that can answer
HAT = test-point altitude - HOT
entity-relative: the HOST aircraft's altitude (Entity Control) - the
request's Z offset (+Z points down; entity axes are NED)
geodetic: the request carries its own altitude
Valid = 0 - never a fabricated 0 m - when no source can cover the point: an
entity other than the ownship (0), an entity-relative request with no
anchor, or a point no source can reach
updatePeriod = 0 -> answered once; n -> re-answered every n-th frame until a
fresh request with the same HAT/HOT ID replaces it (answered at once)
the geodetic FSUIPC fallback is accepted only within 500 m of the aircraft
ANCHOR entity-relative answers are anchored to the HOST's own Entity Control
(entity 0) - the pose its flight model is commanding - not to the sim's
FSUIPC read-back. All-zero and off-globe poses are refused, not adopted.
The six probe offsets are identical wherever the aircraft is, so a stuck
anchor is invisible on the wire: on the rig it parked the aircraft on the
departure ground, a ~550 ft step at the destination.
--terrain-offset applies to the database only: a height from the sim needs no calibration, and applying it would correct it twice. Entity-relative
answers are given at the HOST's aircraft position - the reference capture's six points sit within 10.4 m of it, far below any terrain source's resolution
- and the sim is still asked for the exact point.
5 - The probe tick ladder
Something has to call the free-standing surface query, and it has to keep
running while the aircraft is being positioned. Three ticks, tried in order:
1 - EVENTID_Frame, Prepar3D's per-frame event (IEventServiceV510/V600)
once per rendered frame: the tick of a running sim. v5 keeps signalling it while paused; the rig's v6 does not - pausing stops the frame loop
too.
2 - the object's ISimulation::Update
used until a frame event has been seen, and again if one stops arriving; Update() defers while the frame event is live, so the two never both
service the table
3 - a thread of the add-on's own - the last resort
started at DLLStart, stopped and waited for at DLLStop; steps in only after both ticks above have been silent for kWatchGraceMs = 1000 ms.
It calls QuerySurfaceElevation and nothing else of Prepar3D's.
A running sim never reaches the thread, so the one call made outside Prepar3D's thread can only happen while Prepar3D's own loop has
stopped - which is what the rig does for the whole session. The object-tick lifecycle fault (a reposition stranding the tick) is gone with it.
diag word (bit 31 kPresent must be set; a 0 means "no diagnosis")
0..7 user-object create callbacks (saturate at 255)
8..15 removals of the tick's object
16..23 RegisterSimulation failures
24 a simulation is bound
25 the bound object was the user object then
26 a user-object create was ignored (already bound)
27 the newest pass came from the ADD-ON'S OWN THREAD
31 the word is filled
tail frameTicks frame-event callbacks seen
simEvents bit 0 paused now; sticky pause/unpause, sim
stop/start, scenario load, vehicle change, frozen
simMode GetMode() at the last object tick
frameFails frame-event registration failures
ticks advancing + bit 27 normal for a paused sim, not a fault
ticks frozen, frameTicks > 0 the whole add-on has stopped running
ticks frozen, frameTicks = 0 no frame event was ever delivered
alive clear no surface service at all
6 - Shared-memory contract (src\TerrainProbeIpc.h)
mapping Local\CigiStarter.TerrainProbe.v1 (session-local: both sides run in
the logged-on user's session, so Global\ would need elevation)
magic 'PTBP' (0x50425450) version 2 capacity 256 slots
header (48 B)
magic - version - capacity - tickRateHz
alive 1 while a service and a tick exist
lastError the last HRESULT the probe saw
probePid Prepar3D's pid (what tasklist /m finds)
ticks heartbeat: advances while the probe runs
reqSeq bumped by the IG once it has written queries[]
rspSeq seqlock over results[]: odd while rows are rewritten
queryFails points Prepar3D has refused
diag the diagnostic word (0 = an older add-on)
queries[256] x 32 B the IG writes: latDeg lonDeg altMeters key enabled
results[256] x 48 B the probe writes: latDeg lonDeg hotMeters key status
materialCode nrmAzimuthDeg nrmElevationDeg
tail (16 B) frameTicks simEvents simMode frameFails
1 the IG writes queries[i] (enabled, with its own key), then bumps reqSeq
2 the probe walks the table on its next tick, asks the surface query for every
enabled point and writes results[], the batch guarded by rspSeq
3 the IG accepts a row when status = Ok, the key matches and the echoed lat/lon
still match the point it asked about
-> a one-tick-old answer is safe; a request that has moved is refused and
falls back, never answered with somebody else's terrain
pack(8) plus a static_assert on every size and offset: a differently packed build would agree on slot 0 and misread every slot after it, so a layout
change must bump kVersion. The table is metric - the wire is metres and only the probe converts to the PDK's radians and feet. 256 slots because
TerrainBaker fills the whole table to bake a tile in seconds.
The contract test overrides the mapping name on purpose: sharing it would make its first memset wipe a live add-on's header, which then reads as a
probe that is loaded but has stopped answering.
7 - Operator window
| HOST 192.168.70.2:8001 -> SOF destination |
| Stream : RUNNING (paced to the HOST) |
| SOF rate : 150 Hz requested, 150/s measured |
| SOF frames: 101 |
| Received : 0 datagrams (0/s), 0 entity updates |
| IG mode : 0 (Standby) <- commanded by the HOST |
| HOST frame: 0 |
| Relay : 4 clients, 4 reachable, 1567 datagrams forwarded |
| Relay NIC : Killer E2600 Gigabit Ethernet Controller |
| TerrainDB : 2 tile(s), 1 in memory, 25 MB |
| HAT/HOT : answering from the sim's own terrain |
| Probe : sim paused; the probe is answering from its own |
| thread |
| Anchor : HOST Entity Control -6.53973, 106.75963, 576 ft |
| Terrain : 89 ft ground under the sim aircraft, 99 ft sim |
| aircraft |
| [x] Answer HAT/HOT SOF rate: [ 150 ] Hz [ Apply ] |
| [x] Pace SOF to HOST replies (flow control) |
| [ START ] [ STOP ] [ EXIT ] |
Refreshes 4x/s. START / STOP start and stop the SOF stream (the button that would be a no-op is the disabled one). Answer HAT/HOT also starts and
stops the FSUIPC poller: off means no FSUIPC calls at all. Pace SOF to HOST replies is the flow-control switch. SOF rate is 1..100000 Hz, applied to
the transmit loop on the next frame with Apply or Enter, so the stream retunes while it runs; --fps only seeds it.
EXIT is the only way out: SC_CLOSE is deleted from the system menu (the X is drawn greyed out), WM_CLOSE is ignored, and with no console Ctrl+C
cannot reach it. The stream is already running when the window appears and the window minimises itself; --no-auto-start is the single way back to a
window that waits for the button.
Terrain lines: HAT/HOT names the source in force; TerrainDB the fallback behind it and its size; Probe the tick that is answering; Anchor the HOST's
pose; Terrain the sim's own aircraft over FSUIPC - the ground under it and its altitude in feet, the way Prepar3D shows them.
8 - Fan-out to the extra IG PCs
# one address per line, optional port (default: the IG port, 8000)
client.txt sits beside the executable and is read once at startup. Blank lines, # comments and a Notepad BOM are tolerated; IPv4 only. Junk, a
port of 0 or above 65535, duplicates and this PC's own addresses are skipped and counted. Capped at 32 clients; with no usable line nothing is
relayed and the capture driver is never opened.
per datagram only datagrams whose source is the HOST, copied before
anything is parsed, so a copy is exact
one hand-built Ethernet + IPv4 + UDP frame per client, injected with
pcap_sendpacket; both checksums are computed, the UDP one over the IP
pseudo-header, so a copy is a complete valid datagram
Ethernet dst = the client's MAC src = THIS adapter's own MAC
(spoofing that as well would teach every switch on the
way that the HOST lives on this port)
IP src = the HOST, dst = the client
UDP src = the HOST's port, dst = the client's port
unicast: one frame per client, never broadcast
client MACs are resolved with SendARP on a background thread and
re-resolved every few seconds, so a client switched on or replaced later
is picked up on its own; one that stops answering drops out and the
window counts how many are reachable
datagrams over 1472 B of payload are dropped and counted: a client's
capture filter matches one datagram, not a fragment chain
the adapter is found automatically - the one that owns the IG address,
else whichever the route to the HOST leaves by - and the window names it
relay counts: forwarded = reached at least one client, dropped = reached
none; clients that have not answered yet are neither
Needs Npcap (wpcap.dll), loaded at run time rather than linked, so a PC without it still builds and runs as a plain IG; nothing here needs elevation.
The SOF link to the HOST is unaffected when the adapter cannot be opened.
9 - SOF rate and flow control
The HOST owns the frame rate: one datagram per SOF, and its own frame counter advances about 53 times a second while the reference Master's
SOF ran at ~100 Hz (an 8/12 ms alternation) - the Master asked for roughly twice the replies the HOST had frames to give.
SOF rate default 150 Hz: every answer carries a fresh attitude (the position
comes on every other one), so how often the IG asks is how smoothly the
aircraft moves.
FLOW CONTROL (default on, src\SofPacer.h): a SOF is held back while the previous
one is still unanswered, so the stream fits whatever the HOST on site can
absorb, whatever number is typed in the rate box. A held-back frame is
dropped, never replayed, so no mode of operation can turn the stream into a
burst.
- a HOST that has never answered (startup, not yet woken) is transmitted
to at the full rate
- a SOF unanswered for 100 ms is followed by another anyway, so a HOST that
has dropped out still receives something to wake up on
- the limit is wall-clock, not a count of frames: a HOST answering less than
once per 100 ms sees at most ~10 requests a second whether the box says
150 or 6000. Counting frames would scale the retries with the rate -
exactly the runaway this exists to prevent
The SOF's only live field is the HOST's frame counter echoed at offset 8. An IG-side count would drift from the HOST by (rate - 53) frames a second,
which is what broke it above ~60 Hz. The window's Stream line names the mode - paced to the HOST or free-running - and adds "which is the limit"
when it is the HOST setting the pace; --no-flow-control transmits on the rate alone, as the reference Master did.
10 - Terrain database (SRTM fallback)
terrain\ beside the executable, or --terrain-dir. Raw SRTM .hgt, one
1 x 1 degree cell per file, named by the corner it starts at:
S07E106.hgt covers 7..6 S, 106..107 E (Jakarta)
S08E112.hgt covers 8..7 S, 112..113 E (Surabaya)
SRTMGL1 (1 arc-sec, ~30 m, 3601x3601) and SRTMGL3 (3 arc-sec, ~90 m,
1201x1201) are both accepted; the sample count comes from the file size
samples are signed 16-bit big-endian metres; row 0 is the northern edge
and column 0 the western edge; -32768 is a void (interpolated around, or
reported invalid when a point has nothing but voids)
bilinear between the four surrounding samples; a tile is read in on first
use and kept - the window's TerrainDB line shows indexed / in memory / MB
Two ways to get them. tools\get_terrain.ps1 downloads from the public AWS skadi mirror (-Points "-6.13,106.66" or -Tiles S07E106,S08E112), about 25
MB per 1 arc-sec tile, so fetch only the box the aircraft flies in: the generic world model, quick, but SRTM predates the scenery. tools\TerrainBaker
overlays the simulator's own ground heights on that base - plan -> probe -> survey -> compose -> terrain-sim\*.hgt - sim-exact at the fields, runway
flattening and all (probe/survey need Prepar3D with the add-on loaded; plan and compose need neither).
Calibration: SRTM heights are orthometric (EGM96) and the sim's datum is its own; the two matched to ~2 m at Juanda in testing. --terrain-offset <m>
shifts every database height if a site shows a constant bias - the database only, never FSUIPC and never a sim height.
11 - Build, files and bench tooling
BUILD
msbuild CigiStarter.sln /p:Configuration=Release /p:Platform=x64
-> x64\Release\CigiStarter.exe (x64 only)
GUI subsystem (SubSystem=Windows + EntryPointSymbol=mainCRTStartup)
with a plain int main(): no console, so --help, --version and startup
errors use a message box
static CRT (/MT): a fresh IG PC needs no Visual C++ redistributable
no /GL: FSUIPCuser64.lib is an LTCG library built with MSVC v140
(WholeProgramOptimization=false; expect a benign LNK4098)
runs unelevated (asInvoker) - it starts from a logon path, where a
UAC prompt would block an unattended IG
vendored SDKs: external\UIPC64_SDK_C_version2,
external\npcap-sdk-1.16, external\Prepar3D-SDK\inc\PDK
(/p:FsuipcSdkDir, /p:NpcapSdkDir, /p:P3DSdkDir)
FILES src\main.cpp src\SofPacer.h src\Gui.h/.cpp src\cigi.h/.cpp
src\TerrainSource.h/.cpp the FSUIPC poller thread
src\TerrainDb.h/.cpp the SRTM .hgt reader
src\TerrainProbe.h/.cpp this side of the shared-memory link
src\TerrainProbeIpc.h the pinned contract
src\Relay.h/.cpp client.txt, frames, Npcap, SendARP
client.txt / terrain\ optional inputs beside the exe
BENCH tools\test-hathot-emulator.ps1 -Local [-Stop] -> PASS/FAIL
tools\capture-hat-hot.ps1 [-Summary]
external\HostEmulator_Win32_v3.3.3\Hemu3.exe (Boeing TSS)
tools\PdkTerrainProbe\test\PdkTerrainProbeTest.exe
tools\TerrainBaker plan / probe / survey / compose
captures need Npcap + Wireshark's dumpcap and tshark
PdkTerrainProbe is deliberately not in the solution: it needs the sim's SDK, and a machine that only builds the IG should not be broken by that. The
v5 and v6 DLLs are built separately and kept side by side in bin\Release-v5 and bin\Release-v6.
